openIssues.title: Webhook retry backoff too aggressive under regional failover
openIssues.affectedRate: Delivery delay up to 90s during failover windows only
openIssues.description: When a region fails health checks and traffic reroutes, queued webhook retries back off further than necessary before the new region is confirmed healthy, adding avoidable delivery latency.
openIssues.workaround: None needed for most integrations — events still deliver, just later than normal during failover. Partners polling the Ban API directly are unaffected.

openIssues.title: Gen-2 driver falls back to legacy attestation on some AMD AGESA 1.2.0.3 boards
openIssues.affectedRate: ~1.4% of alpha-channel sessions, all on X670/X870 boards with AGESA 1.2.0.3
openIssues.description: With VBS enabled, the boot-chain attestation reads an inconsistent PCR 7 value on these firmware revisions. The driver detects the mismatch and downgrades to the 0.5.x attestation path rather than failing the session — protection is unchanged, only the attestation report is marked "legacy".
openIssues.workaround: None required. Partners who need full attestation on these boards can keep the affected titles on the 0.5.x beta channel until the fix ships.

openIssues.title: Zero-Footprint Mode preview delays the second scan cycle on hybrid CPUs
openIssues.affectedRate: Opt-in preview only — up to 400 ms added to the second scan cycle on Intel hybrid parts
openIssues.description: Re-mapping the scan engine after the first unmap occasionally lands on an E-core and misses its timing budget once. Subsequent cycles are unaffected. This is why the mode ships as opt-in in the alpha.
openIssues.workaround: Leave Zero-Footprint Mode disabled (the default) for titles where the first minute of a session is latency-critical.

openIssues.title: Thunderbolt DMA path check can flag eGPU enclosures as unattested devices
openIssues.affectedRate: Laptops with an external GPU over Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 — flagged for review, never auto-banned
openIssues.description: The new external PCIe tunnel enumeration treats an eGPU enclosure whose firmware is not yet in the fingerprint database as an unknown DMA-capable device. Sessions are routed to manual review, not auto-ban, so no player has been banned by this.
openIssues.workaround: Partners can allowlist enclosure vendor IDs under Settings → Detection Tuning → PCIe Allowlist while enclosure firmware is added to the database.
openIssues.targetFix: Firmware database update — no driver release needed
